title: Supernova Agent or Editor MCP: Which to Use for What
summary: Supernova Agent works inside Supernova; Editor MCP works from your own AI tool. Which to use for each job, what each costs in credits, and when to use both.
body_markdown:
"We already connected Editor MCP to[Cursor](https://cursor.com/) . Do we need the agent too?"


It's a fair question since[Supernova Agent](https://www.supernova.io/blog/introducing-supernova-agent) went into public beta on 26 October. Both can write to your design system. Both document components, clean up tokens, link[Figma](https://www.figma.com/) and publish. So which one is for what?


The short answer: **Supernova Agent** is for work you do inside Supernova. **Editor MCP** is for work that starts in your own AI tool or touches other tools as well. Most teams that maintain a design system will end up using both.


## What's the difference, in one table?


**Supernova Agent** is an AI agent built into Supernova. You open it from the side navigation and describe the job. **[Editor MCP](https://www.supernova.io/blog/introducing-supernova-editor-mcp)** is an MCP server that gives the AI tool you already use write access to the same design system data.


Supernova Agent Editor MCP


Where it runs Inside Supernova In Cursor,[Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) ,[Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) ,[VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) or[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/)


Setup None Add` https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp` as a connector and sign in


Context Whatever page, token or component you have open, attached automatically What you tell it, plus any other MCP servers you've connected


Design systems Several in one conversation One per connector (add a connector per design system)


Files Attach CSVs, PDFs, screenshots, Word and Excel files Whatever your AI tool can read


Who can use it Contributor, Editor, Admin, Owner Contributor and above


Cost 50 workspace credits per message Reads free; 3 credits per change, 5 for heavy changes


Sources:[Agent 101](https://learn.supernova.io/latest/ai/agent/agent-101-8UfCrOf2) ,[Editor MCP](https://learn.supernova.io/latest/ai/mcp/editor-mcp-zZuzFobd) and[Workspace credits](https://learn.supernova.io/latest/settings/workspace/billing/workspace-credits-QppYjvRr) on Supernova Learn, checked 5 November 2026. Both are in beta and the credit costs may change.


Both act as the signed-in user, with that user's permissions. Both wait for your confirmation before they publish or delete anything.


The Academy lesson shows the agent on five everyday jobs, from token descriptions to a deprecation:


## Which should you use for each job?


Pick by where the work starts and where its inputs live.


Job Use Why


"Which token should I use for error text?" Agent You're already in Supernova, and it answers from what you have open


Write the Checkbox page in your house style Agent It reads your other component pages without you pointing at them


Bulk rename` space-1…space-8` to` space-xs…space-3xl` Either One prompt in both; the agent shows each change as a chip you can open


Create colour tokens from a CSV Agent Attach the file to the chat


Migrate docs from[zeroheight](https://zeroheight.com/) or[Confluence](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence) Editor MCP Your AI tool can hold both connections and move content between them


Document a component from its code Editor MCP The agent in your editor can read the repo and write to Supernova in the same session


Audit before a release Agent "List documentation pages that are blank or nearly empty", then fix in the same chat


Change several design systems in one go Agent One conversation can cover several; Editor MCP needs a connector for each


The pattern behind the table: if every input is already in Supernova, the agent saves you the setup and the context-pasting. If an input lives in a repo, another docs tool or another MCP server, Editor MCP is the bridge.


This one shows the other side: your design system reached from the AI tools your team already uses.


## What does each cost for the same job?


The two are priced differently. The agent charges **per message** , whatever the message does. Editor MCP charges **per change** , and reading is free. That makes small, frequent questions cheaper through Editor MCP. Larger jobs done in one message can come out about even.


Three examples, using the published rates:


- **One question ("Where is Card documented?"):** Agent, 50 credits. Editor MCP, 0 credits, because it only reads.
- **Rename eight space tokens:** Agent, 50 credits for one message. Editor MCP, 24 credits if the rename runs as eight separate token updates at 3 each, or less if it runs as one bulk action.
- **Write one component page, then two rounds of edits:** Agent, 150 credits for three messages. Editor MCP, about 15 credits for three documentation edits at 5 each.


Editor MCP leaves a cost out of that comparison: the AI tool on the other end. Cursor, Claude and ChatGPT bill you separately for their own usage. The agent's 50 credits cover the model as well.


For scale,[Starter](https://www.supernova.io/pricing) includes 1,000 workspace credits a month, about 20 agent messages. Pro includes 10,000, about 200.


## What can't they do?


A few limits worth knowing before you plan work around either one:


- **No one-click undo:** Neither has an undo button yet. Documentation edits show up in page history, so you can restore a page. For anything else, ask for the revert in the same conversation and check the result.
- **Nothing that originates outside Supernova:** Editor MCP can't create Figma components, code components,[Storybook](https://storybook.js.org/) stories or assets. Those come in through their own sources.
- **No workspace administration:** Editor MCP can't create design systems or versions, or change member roles.
- **Viewers get read-only access:** Anyone without Contributor access reads your system through Consumer MCP, which can't make changes.


## Using both together


A split that works well is by phase.


1. **Bring the system in through Editor MCP.** Your AI tool reads the old docs site or the code and writes pages, tokens and components into Supernova.
2. **Maintain it with the agent.** Day-to-day fixes, audits and publishing happen where the system now lives.
3. **Hand the results to coding agents.** The agent can[turn a guidelines page into a skill](https://learn.supernova.io/latest/ai/agent/agent-use-cases-XMOThVRx) , and contexts package what your engineers' agents read through MCP.


That third step is why either tool matters. A guideline written for people tells an agent what to think. Skills, tokens and component data tell it what to output. Both tools spend most of their time keeping that structured layer accurate, which is the part of an[agentic design system](https://www.supernova.io/blog/what-is-an-agentic-design-system) that goes out of date first.


## Start with one job you've been putting off


If you've never used either, open the agent and ask for an audit: "Which documentation pages have never been published?" It needs no setup, and it shows you what changing things in chat feels like.


If your team already lives in Cursor or Claude Code,[connect Editor MCP](https://www.supernova.io/blog/connect-design-system-mcp-claude-code) and give it the migration or code-to-docs job instead.


Pick **Editor MCP** at sign-in to get write access. Consumer MCP is the read-only connection.
